title: Do open permit records predict how long a permit and the build behind it take, better than each city's own averages?
lede: research programme: do open building-permit feeds from several US cities predict permit and build duration; milestone 1 loaded 4.5 million rows from Chicago, San Francisco and Austin onto one schema (median application-to-issue 0 days in Chicago and SF, 6 in Austin); no model run yet
summary: An open research programme on duration forecasting from public building-permit feeds. The proposal has 12 checked works, four falsifiable hypotheses and a time-split evaluation with conformal intervals. Milestone 1 pulled 851,778 Chicago, 1,297,657 San Francisco and 2,382,939 Austin permits onto one schema with datasheets. Descriptive only: median application-to-issue is 0 days in Chicago and San Francisco (90th percentile 56 and 70 days) and 6 days in Austin (90th percentile 176); median issue-to-completion is about 105 days (SF) and 103 days (Austin). Chicago is issued-only, so it is excluded from survivorship-sensitive claims. No model has been run: preliminary.
